The Null Space and the Penalized Coordinates of a Smooth

Source: R/random_smooth.R
dot-random_smooth_split.Rd

Splits the coefficients of a smooth into the directions on which every component of its penalty vanishes and the directions that the penalty covers, and returns the linear map from the smooth's coefficients to those two groups.

Usage

.random_smooth_split(comps, names, tol = 1e-10)

Arguments

comps

The component matrices, as .random_smooth_components() returns them.

names

The smooth's coordinate names, without its label.

tol

The relative eigenvalue tolerance for a zero.

Value

A list with T, the map (\(p\) rows, one column per coordinate of the random effect, null space first); nnull, the dimension of the null space; npen, the number of penalized coordinates; comps, the components on the penalized coordinates; and names.

Details

The null space of a sum of positive semidefinite matrices is the intersection of the components' null spaces, so it is read once from the components normalized to a unit largest entry and does not move with the smoothing parameters.

Where the smoother has already placed the null space in its leading columns with a zero border in every component, as every basis7 smoother does under null_space = "keep", the map keeps those columns and their names. Otherwise, as for a tensor product, an orthonormal basis of the null space and one of its complement are taken from the eigenvectors of the normalized sum, and the columns are named null1, ... and z1, ....

With a single component the penalized coordinates are then whitened: with \(P = R^\top R\) the penalty on the penalized coordinates \(\gamma\), the coordinates \(\delta = R\gamma\) carry the identity penalty, so the random effect over them is independent and Gaussian with one standard deviation. A Demmler-Reinsch smoother already has the identity there, and its coordinates are unchanged. With several components the penalized coordinates are kept and each component is carried onto them.
